clue.text: Sleep soundly, getting dismissal: it's something you have to bear

indicators.note: soundly here means said out loud, so the word for sleep is taken by its sound only

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
getting the sack is being dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps well despite losing their job, which is a burden to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' seems to mean deeply, but it marks a homophone: NAP is spelt KNAP. Add SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack-style bag is carried on the back, borne by its wearer.

clue.text: Take personal charge to get money?

definitions.text: Take personal charge to get money?

parts.words: Take personal charge to get money?
parts.note: taking charge of a person, literally seizing them, in order to demand a ransom

explanation.surface: Someone takes responsibility in order to earn some cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Abduction for ransom is seizing a person to extract money.

clue.text: With general consent it's a deadly sin

parts.note: greed (avarice) is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Everyone agrees that something is a mortal sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled by common accord, everybody having assented.

clue.text: Coy about unusual material

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for coy surrounds the other piece

parts.note: coy means shy
unusual means odd

explanation.surface: A bashful person is wary of some strange fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: SHODDY is also a cloth made from recycled wool, the sense the definition uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is a cheap fabric woven from shredded rags and reclaimed wool.

clue.text: Took charge of conservative, not terribly moved

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: rolled means moved along

explanation.surface: A Tory who was quite unmoved took command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not terribly' reads as 'not very', but 'terribly' rearranges NOT into ONT.
explanation.definitionFit: Directed or managed something, exercising command over it.

clue.text: Hold yours to restrain Arabs?

parts.note: plays on the saying 'hold your ...' meaning wait, with Arabs as a breed of steed to be held back

explanation.surface: Advice to wait patiently before restraining some Arabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabs are a breed of riding animal, and 'hold your horses' means be patient.

clue.text: Almost defeated batsman is scoring?

definitions.meaning: fleeing, in retreat, close to being beaten
in cricket a batsman scoring runs is running between the wickets

explanation.definitionFit: Being pursued and in flight is near defeat; a cricketer taking runs is literally running.

clue.text: Sentimentality that's shown by Henry at zenith, drinking whisky

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so the other letters surround the drink

parts.note: SC (scilicet) is the abbreviation meaning 'that is' or 'namely'
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Z is an abbreviation for zenith
malt is a kind of whisky

explanation.surface: A boozy scene of mawkishness involving a man called Henry at his peak.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, H and Z surround MALT, which goes in after SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmaltz is cloying, excessive emotional sweetness in art or music.

clue.text: Stone roads running by under US city

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed after
running suggests the letters flow into a new order

parts.note: NY is New York
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'by' (three by four)

explanation.surface: Stony roads run beneath an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges ROADS to SARDO; X goes under NY in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a gemstone, a banded form of onyx with sard.

clue.text: Artful Dodger on the river

indicators.note: artful means cunning or crafty, hinting the letters are cleverly reworked

explanation.surface: The Artful Dodger, Dickens's pickpocket, is out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is a boy pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist; 'Artful' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dordogne is a major river in south-west France.

clue.text: One bringing fellow away from engraver

indicators.note: away from means the fellow's letter is taken out of the other word

parts.note: a fetcher is someone who brings things

explanation.surface: Someone escorting a man away from an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who cuts designs into metal plates with acid is an engraver.

clue.text: In mining town have existence after bread is distributed

indicators.note: after places the existence word behind the rearranged letters
distributed means spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: are means exist (we are)

explanation.surface: Life in a pit village after the bread ration is handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: BREAD rearranged gives ABERD, followed by ARE. ABERDARE is a former coal town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdare is a Welsh valley town built on coal mining.

clue.text: Start and keep going over the story of ice-cream

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the start word houses the other piece

parts.note: go means start (ready, steady, go)

indicators.note: going over suggests turning around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: Begin and carry on recounting the tale of a frozen dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE reversed is ELAT, kept inside GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelato is the Italian style of ice-cream.

clue.text: A rotter upset me with current state of learning

parts.note: a cad is a rotter

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
Cal is an abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A scoundrel distresses me with the present condition of education.
explanation.walkthrough: ME upset gives EM. 'state of learning' looks like the definition, but 'state' is CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Academical means relating to academies, universities and scholarship.

clue.text: Motherland of Assyria?

parts.note: a phrase for one's homeland, applied to an ancient vanished empire

explanation.surface: Asking where an ancient empire's homeland lies.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant's homeland is called this, and Assyria is an ancient nation.

clue.text: Thinks pictures will keep popular

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the pictures word houses the other piece

parts.note: images are pictures
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone believes photographs will stay fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposes or pictures in the mind.

clue.text: All right city to house graduate in US state

parts.note: OK means all right
LA is Los Angeles
MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: An American city agrees to give a home to a graduate.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty states, in the south-central US.

clue.text: A French sleeper that will never rise to the level of consciousness?

definitions.text: A French sleeper that will never rise to the level of consciousness?

parts.words: A French sleeper that will never rise to the level of consciousness?
parts.note: a sleeper here is a sleeping car on a continental train, not a person who might wake up

explanation.surface: A dozing Frenchman who will never wake up.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a sleeping car on a European railway.

clue.text: Reformed Madam's keen to restore status quo

indicators.note: reformed means made into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its S as written

explanation.surface: A brothel-keeper who has gone straight is eager to put things right.
explanation.walkthrough: A madam runs a brothel; 'Reformed' suggests she has changed her ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Compensating for a wrong puts things back as they were.

clue.text: Keep busy vessel in old Cyprus

indicators.note: in places the vessel inside the other letters

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
a cup is a drinking vessel

explanation.surface: A ship stays busy in the waters off Cyprus of old.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage someone's time or attention fully.

clue.text: Severely criticise a mother's millinery?

parts.note: to pan is to slate a show or book
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Slating a mum's hat shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: a Panama is a straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight straw hat, an item of headwear.

clue.text: Adorn, with notes, 52 cards

parts.note: B and E are musical notes
a deck is a full pack of 52 playing cards

explanation.surface: Decorating a pack of cards with musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate or festoon.

clue.text: Before August lad brought back fertilisers

indicators.note: brought back means each word is turned around in its place

parts.note: a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy came home before the end of summer with bags of manure.
explanation.walkthrough: Each piece is turned in place: AUG gives GUA and SON gives NOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Guano is bird droppings used to fertilise crops.

clue.text: Keep vital stuff from head of espionage and friend around CIA

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the following word
around means the friend's letters enclose the agency's

parts.note: mate means friend

explanation.surface: Starving a spy chief and comrade of vital supplies around the CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve, making a body waste away through lack of food.

clue.text: Food for simpleton

definitions.meaning: a type of pasta or Asian strand of dough

explanation.definitionFit: A strip of pasta, and a dim fool (also slang for the head).

clue.text: Account by clergyman is precise

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman's report is exact.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and correct.

clue.text: Poor housing worker in attempt to dislodge coconut?

indicators.note: in places the worker inside the other word

parts.note: a coconut shy is a fairground stall where balls are thrown at coconuts; a shy is a throw
an ant is a worker

explanation.surface: Someone toiling in a slum tries knocking down a coconut.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground game of throwing balls to knock coconuts off stands.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude hut, the dwelling of the poor.

clue.text: Repeat drama has returned

parts.note: a play is a drama
back means returned (he is back)

explanation.surface: A theatre production has come back.
explanation.definitionFit: Replaying recorded sound or video.
